content: The test image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, scattered orange-yellow to brick-red raised pustules across the green surface. Top candidates: **Southern rust**, **Common rust**, and **Eyespot**. Let me compare reference images.

**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Corn leaf (upper surface) with numerous small, round, orange-yellow to golden-orange scattered dots/pustules
- Slight yellowish halos around many of the spots
- Dense but not coalescing — still discrete
- No elongated lesion shape, no discrete bullseye rings, no dark black structures

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Southern rust**: Upper-left panel of reference shows identical scattered golden-orange dots on green leaf — perfect match in color, size, density, and distribution pattern
- **Common rust**: Pustules are darker cinnamon-brown, more elongated, and more visibly raised/eruptive — doesn't match
- **Eyespot**: Shows prominent yellow halos forming complete concentric rings around a dark center (bullseye) — test image lacks this well-defined ring pattern; spots are more pustule-like
- **Holcus spot**: Large white/tan circular spots with brown margins — clearly different
- **Tar spot**: Small raised black/dark stromata — clearly different

The test image's orange-yellow color, small round pustule appearance, upper leaf surface concentration, and scattered distribution all match **Southern rust** in early-to-moderate stage.
